title: Moki & Julio: One switch, three Wi-Fi bands - a 1-bit polarisation-rotating RIS cell (simulation study)
description: Simulation study (Palace full-wave FEM + exact network algebra; nothing built or measured) of one 15 mm, 1-bit, polarisation-rotating reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) cell whose single shared switch state covers the 2.4-2.4835 GHz and 5.15-7.125 GHz Wi-Fi bands. Four PIN diodes, each in series with a 0201 chip inductor, on one copper layer over an air spacer, with a raised ground boss and short via that suppress an oblique-incidence centre-charging resonance. Worst-case loss over a realistic parts box (diode spread, inductor tolerance, 0.013-0.017 pF mounting capacitance) is 0.81-0.91 dB at normal incidence and at most 1.37 dB to 45 deg along the cell edges and 30 deg along the diagonal; 45 deg along the diagonal misses 2 dB (2.21 / 2.28 dB). The 180 +- 20 deg bit target is met only at normal incidence with typical parts in 5-7 GHz; the report explains why (mounting capacitance, a non-Foster requirement, the diagonal sheet-scaling limit) and gives a lower-capacitance diode option. The tables and every computed number are regenerated by the included scripts from the included network files; vendor files are not redistributed. Design, text, figures and data: CC BY 4.0; code: MIT (LICENSE-CODE).
